So I've got about 100 legitimate hours of playing this game. That's split between playing the singleplayer, building ships for tournaments, watching my ships compete in tournaments, and sharing and battling ships with friends.
This is, in all honesty, one of the best space-ship games I've ever played. The game itself is built on very simple components: simple physics, simple graphics, and simple 2-D exploration. However, it is the way these parts fit together under the fantastic music and brilliant vector-based combat that just draw you in. Very immersive, very fun, very addicting, and by far the best ship builder in any space game I've ever played. The ship builder and sharing tools are really the highlights of the game.
What there is to do:
-Build ships from scratch
-Fly ships in open 2D space
-explore procedurally generated content (As with all games that rely on procedurally generated content, the wow factor goes away pretty fast. Thankfully, this isn't what the game relies on to stay fun)
-Unlock new ship pieces and build better ships out of the scrap of your defeated foes.
-Build a factory and begin constructing a fleet
- Battle fleets made by other players at hotly contested wormholes (There is no multiplayer, but the AI is VERY good and it pilots the fleets that players themselves upload. It priotizes the fleets made by steam friends)
-Enter the wormhole to upload your fleet
-share ship.lua files with friends and pit them in 1v1 battle in tournament mode to see who can make the best ship.
-7 playable factions
That's about it. One last note, it seems that the developer is pretty much done with the game. There haven't been any major patches since the launch and the forum activity has died down quite a bit, but I believe the last thing that's being set up for this game is compatibility with steam workshop so that all future content will come from the game's players rather than the devs.

If you like construction and customization, building a fleet of ships, leading your fleet into huge battles with other players' fleets for the sake of expanding your galactic empire, buy this game.
Don't let the 2d vector graphics throw you off. Reassembly is a relaxing game with a great soundtrack, infinite creativity, and great battles.
Several different factions, all with a different selection of weapons and hull blocks, gives much more replayability and keeps the gameplay from getting repetetive. The real fun is the ship building, though. Test your ships in simulated battles against other players' designs, and then use them in the game.
Basically if you ever dreamed of building and commanding a fleet of spaceships, you will love this game.
Solid Civilization-style gameplay, with much more interesting combat mechanics and and interesting lore snuck in.
A really great game to sit down, gather round your friends and see what happens.

Where to start-
Reassembly is a top down 2D action spaceship building/ combat game. Sadly thats all it is though. This does not mean the game doesnt have some fun in it! You can encounter other players ships and send your fleet out for others to find. You will fly through space collecting resources and fighting other ships. It reminds me alot of first stage of SPORE. Ships out and about everywhere, collecting to power up.... Then some behemoth comes along and kills everyone.
Pros-
- Easy to use builder. Doesnt take long to build ships.
- Decent combat. Sometimes the AI is wonky but all in all good.
- Huge areas to explore. Though after a couple times it feels the same.
- Neat factions each with their own strengths, except 3. Faction 3 is wet tissue paper hanging on toothpicks. Dont hit a rock too hard or bye bye ship.
- Good ship physics. How you build your ship completely affects the way it moves. Only complaint here is the seemingly never ending drift.
- General fun gathering. If you like the first stage of the game SPORE you will enjoy this.
Cons-
- Ship building is somewhat limited. You cant make really huge ships. This is limited by the max 8000P also once they reach a certain size the ether have no speed or no guns.
- Combat is decent but thats all there is to the game. Collect, size up, fight.
- Agents. I love the fact I find other peoples ships, I dont love that sometimes I run into massive fleet 10 mins in that destroys me so hard space rips a new black hole!!
- Some factions are unbalanced. Faction 3 is so soft on the hull that most my deaths came from hitting something too hard. I know it says hard mode but come on now tissue paper is not hull material. Faction 1 and 2 have the most building options. 4 can become really strong really fast. Like cut ships in half kinda strong. After playing all the factions I find 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 left me feeling let down. They didnt have as much to work with as 1 and 2 or were just 1 trick gimmick factions.
-Not all factions are playable. While you can mod to make them so, they are incomplete. I would love to see the borg like faction become playable or the plant type.
-Nothing but combat. I already mentioned this but it really is the biggest issue. Litterally all you do is collect, size up, fight, repeat. The game needs something.
All in all id say 4/5 stars. Sure it has alot of downs but that did not stop me from spending 40 hours surfing the stars. I recommend this to anyone who loved the first level of SPORE. If you liked that you will like this.

Greetings, I just replayed this game and I must say that it is still an enjoyable experience.  In many ways this game feels more like a documentary of gaming history than a standalone game.  Regardless of that it is a lot of fun.
Nostalgia:  This game pulls at the strings of not only the evolution of technology but also the evolution of RPGs.  The mechanics themselves may not be that original (or even at all, as I feel it is the intention) but they are done well and with precision.  This is one of few games that I won’t complain about precision of mechanics and controls as they are spot on.
Old but New:  This game does an amazing job at presenting the various game designs of the games they tribute; the sound is solid and the graphics feel clean but within their genre.  I do wish there was more however as there is really only about 3-5 hours of play.
A Story not told:  The story is more or less non-existent, the atmosphere is there and yes there is a story but you don’t really care and there isn’t much to follow; but to be honest, this isn’t an issue.  An amazingly deep story is not why you are here; you are here to relive your childhood or to at least appreciate the progression of RPGs.
Overall, if you are a gamer you should get this game.  If you want to live through the history, get this game.  Really I feel this is a lesson in our history that every player should participate in, even if it is just done for learning and not for the gaming purpose.  Yes, you only get 5 hours about but it is short enough to hold your attention but long enough to demonstrate everything well.  Enjoy!

I've played this game quite intesively when I had this for the original Xbox. Just recently got this game not too long ago. Haven't had much time playing the game, but I know that I had a blast.
The game is based on a time period way before the original Star Wars movies, retelling the times of when the Republic was not just clones, but real actual people, similar to how the Rebels are. The story is based on the conflict between the Sith and the Republic as you, someone who is "supposively" a Republic soldier goes on his path to make himself heard in the world. The plot goes through quite a bit of twists and turns, as people you see around you are not who they say they are.
As you progress through the story through the class RPG style, kill things, do quests and advance through, you'll discover many new skills and powers that will be beneficial to how you wish to transverse through the universe. Do you wish to be stealth like and assasinate? Do you want to be a center of attention and tank any and all damage directed to you? Do you want to be a martksman that eliminates enemies from a distance? Whatever you want to do, the game allows adequate progression through any method you desire.
The combat and main concept of the game revolves around a turn-based, yet real time based fighting style, in which you can queue up actions and moves to eliminate enemies or complete objectives. However, you're able to pause and plan out certain movements as a way of micro-management, to prevent the deaths of your party members. At any given time, you can have up to two other party members, each of which you have found on your journey, who all have their own strengths and weaknesses in battle and outside of it.
Additionally, the game has a morality or "Light/Dark" meter that is based on your actions in game. If you kill people instead of sparing their lives, you'll gain dark side points and vice-versa. With this, two different endings can occur, making a replay a worthwile investment.
Like most Star Wars games, the enviroments and art-styles are amazing, even if the graphics are still dated. With different moods and lightings, climates and habitats, you'll find each and every planet you visit something completely different.
Overall, this game has been an amazing experience in my childhood, no matter how little patience I had for the game. If you're looking for an amazing Star Wars game that'll leave you guessing and amazing, Star Wars: KoTOR is definitely the game for you.

Gameplay: The game provides you with three things at the start. A gun, a flashlight, and a motion tracker. You work your way through an empty ship and narrow corridors  that gradually become overflowed with beasts. Your objective is to download datacores, deactivate the coolant for the reactor, and escape before meltdown.

-Aspects: Depending on your game options you are given a few defenses to your disposal. These consist of Doors, Sentries, and Laser doors. Each plays a vital game changing role once used, however if you're not smart about it, every single one of them can kill you just as easily as it does protect you.
Mechanics: Though sparse, they are unique. The game is built to feel like an arcade shooter. The more you progress, the better upgrades you get. your gun gets stronger, your flashlight gets brighter, you get aim assist which highlights enemies in view, and can even obtain infravision making problems of darkness a thing of the past at the cost of increased battery drain when in use.
Again depending on your game options, different things can happen. Beasts can be set to spawn in certain conditions or can be set to spawn at pure random locations for a greater challenge. Thre are small enemies called creeps which can obstruct your view and damage your armor. Anything that damages your armor will take away one visual indicator whether it be ammo count. your flashlight, or even your objective. such can be repaired at repair stations. Not to mention the newly added possibility of power going completely dead leaving you to the beasts in pitch black darkness, your muzzle flash being your best source of light.
In Conclusions, this is the Scariest pacman game I've ever played in my life.

Essential purchase for any English-speaker with a sense of humour. The extremely low price makes it a must-buy. The game itself would easily sell for a higher price. This game goes down an absolute storm with friends or at parties.
This works very much like a 2 player card game. You go head to head against your opponent (campaign, Online multiplayer, and local co-op) and the aim is to build up the biggest and most brutal insults you can, to humiliate your opponent into eventual submission, whilst there are many nuances (chaining combos over multiple turns, character weaknesses and more) to the game which force you to think tactically and weigh up risk vs reward. It's fairly straightforward, but a lot of fun, and carries a great sense of humour. The humour involved is very English, as is the grammar (and some slang terms). The game is simply (but effectively) presented in a uniquely-weird pixel-art fashion. There are a number of interesting characters who are all fully voiced to speak out (almost) any insult you can come up with. Each character has a weakness (for example, references to modern technology, or being old and more). Some crossovers appear here, such as Serious Sam, Lo Wang (Shadow Warrior) which are voiced by the actual guys. There are many references to Monty Python in this game, which I think is done quite nicely. It really does feel like Monty Python: The Game at times.
The only negative thing I can think of about this game is that occasionally some insults can get nonsensical. The vast majority of the time, the game works fairly, rewarding smart, tactical thinking.
Did I mention that the ranked online mode is extremely addictive? There's nothing quite like beating the #1 ranked player...or two of them...

enough complaining about the game, I've given it a positive review so might aswell state why it's still fun rather than just bashing on and on about the problems it has.

the levels were quite well designed. Though it wasn't very clear where to go, I managed to find everything. Maybe add a minimap for directions or see if the brightness alone will fix this problem.
As I'm turning this into a tell the dev what could be done better I'll write down the rest of the things I've got on my mind aswell.

I also noticed in that level when you respawn, you respawn in the air. Probably to not get stuck in the floor but once I respawned it took a few seconds before I landed because of the gravity.
Another thing I noticed is that the orb enemies only showed up once. they came up through the platform which I fell through.
Damn that was a lot of typing... Hopefully that was helpful and dev if you need more playtesting done, just hit me up. I'm known to be good at breaking games ;)

The comic book, and table top inspired world of Champions is brought to life in a game full of character customization, developed story, and steady flow of new content. Although limited by the free service in some aspects- through the use of microtransactions, or the use of the subscription the customization is limited only by your imagination (and your wallet.) If you're looking for a new MMO and enjoy playing the role of superhero/heroine Champions Online is a great start, and you can take comfort in knowing it's only getting better and better.

While Champions Online may not be the best MMO in terms of engaging questlines, there's quite a bit of fun to be had with the character creator alone. Interesting power sets make gameplay fairly diverse, spreading mechanics between familiar melee, ranged, 'tank', 'dps' and 'support' class structures. It's not for everyone, but now that it's free to play it's definitely worth a try.
Do you like Sniper Elite? Do you like making Zombie heads explode? do you like killing Nazi Zombies and possibly ZombHitler? then this game is for you!

One of the great features of this game is that it's turn-based and the players in a match don't need to be online at the same time, as a lot of time can pass in between turns and the match is still active.
Meaning that you could have, say, ten active matches at a certain point, that's twenty cycles (two hours' worth game-time) which you can prime without any the other players being online. If one day you don't have the time, no problem, the match will be waiting when you find the time.
All this game needs at this point is for players to come in and have some PATIENCE.
I started playing 8 months ago and I have managed to play many good matches, but it is a shame that many players come in and don't get that it's turn-based, and they leave thinking the game is completely dead.
You can read what other people think are good or bad aspects of the game, but ultimately it's up to you to try it out for yourself.

Coming from Civilization, I wanted to try something new for a while, and Endless Legend seems to be the answer.
There are some great things in Endless Legend; however, it may not be enough to turn everyone away from CIV.
Starting with the
of Endless:
: It's like Beyone Earth done right.
. RTS style of combat, way better than CIV. And if you start a combat near another army or city, reinenforcements will join the combat as well.
: The heroes will enhance your army in different ways. They also level up. Reminds me of Heroes of Might and Magic. They can also govern your cities for you,
: You can merge upto six units into armies. Your settlers will never be ambushed again.
: You can upgrade weapons and armors on your units. That first unit can still be useful after 200 turns.
: Unlike the city-states in CIV, they give you RPG style quests. And once pacified (allied/befrieded) they can be assimilated into your empire, giving you bonuses and ability to train their units.
of Endless:
: I thought CIV's tutorial is bad enough, but Endless is even worse. You have learn so many things on your own. To make it worse, Endless have a higher learning curve to begin with.
: This can be very annoying if you come from CIV. The map is divided into regions, and you can only have
city in each region. Therefore, if you want that awesome pile of perls thats on the other end of a region. Good luck with that because you need to build wonders or a specific building in order to expand your city. And building too much of that building increases your unhappiness.
: This one is more of a nuisance than a con. The game will proceed if you forgot to research. And the design of the tech tree can be confusing for beginners.
: No specific music, leaders are voice less. And you need a specific resource, "influence", in order to trade. Why?
Overall, this game is great. It's definately worth a try if you enjoy strategy games. However, this is a more traditional strategy games which means much more micro-management. Not for the COD generation.

This game.... is a scary game.
Regularly while playing you hear shrieks of terror over teamspeak when playing with friends, and mark my words. you want to use a voice program. because SBTF leaves you no time to type anything out.
The game has 1-4 players working to destroy an infested space ship or facility, (its got no story so whatever) anyway, so you arrive in your escape pod and move into a series of dark corridoors and rooms, you then try and gather all the datacores and activate the self destruct.
While thats happening, the aliens start breaching into sections of the ship, you try and fight them off while completing objectives.
You can seal breaches and hold the aliens up for a while in certain parts of a map or just use your guns to keep them at bay. this is really up to your map generation settings.
You generate a random map to play on, you can define a seed which lets you see what you are facing or go in blind, you can enable or disable various defensive objects, change the difficulty and even change the level a little using for example, the bigger rooms option.
So, it becomes a crazy hard game of 4 against the swarm when playing with friends or a horrifyingly jumpscare ridden fight for your life in solo.
The games got quite a few interesting features BUT. and heres the sad bit. the games got some issues.
Multiplayer:
the game uses peer to peer multiplayer but because of the way the game handles it... well. its got all the weaknesses and none of the strengths of peer to peer. if a player leaves your game, lags out or gets disconnected, the entire group becomes desynched and the game will either crash or not finish properly, often resulting in odd in game behaviour.
Because all 4 players in a 4 player match are considered server hosts, if one drops out the whole thing falls apart.
Also the game has no drop in ability meaning people must wait to join your group, this means its much harder to find a game to play in as you have to wait until someone is finished to join.
the ability to join and spectate while waiting is sorely needed.
User interface:
the user interface is horrible, and uses no standard conventions, its like someoene just threw together things and didn't think about how to present them usefully.
Changing loadouts after a mission requires clicking on buttons that are named oddly and navigation through menus and settings is just odd.
-Hopefully being early access this will get an update pass at somepoint
Weapons:
lets face it the weapons are workable but some of them are just plain useless without the right ammo. you also have a dupplicated weapon which is just a re-colored copy of another one and it fires powerful shots but so slow that your dead before you get a shot off making it pretty useless unless we get more powerful aliens at some point.
That being said. I like the game, its an old fashion shoot fest which is scary as hell and great fun in a group. its let down a little by the user interface and lack of different mission objectives but they don't stop the game from being fun. and as long as your internet connection is good, you should'nt encounter the most annoying problem with the game.

The game is fun, intense, unique, and runs smoothly while still looking very good, masterfully utilizing the gritty sci-fi aesthetic. The way your visor HUD ties into the gameplay itself is elegantly done and adds to the player's immersion, which compliments the adrenaline-pumping claustrophobic feel the game is going for. It is fast-paced and hectic at times, but still has a strategical element to it, as you can open/close doors, activate defensive measures like lazers and automatic turrets, and so forth, which I imagine comes even more into play in multiplayer. That, however, leads me to my major gripe about the game: the difficulty is incredibly unfair in singleplayer. Now I'm no stranger to hard games, I enjoy an extra challenge, but as a lone marine you will often find yourself in situations where survival is next to impossible, even on the easier difficulty. Enemies spawn in endless numbers and with seemingly no pauses or waves once they really start coming. Seeing as all that bulky space marine armour of yours apparently does little good against ravenous aliens, a single attack by the bigger variant will take you down for good. It is simply not possible to cover all fronts at all times, leading to the outcome of your mission in singleplayer being more up to hoping for the game to generate a very linear level with lots of turrets and safe zones more so than the actual skill of the player. Talking about death, for me personally the game lacks an incentive to keep playing (and dying) over and over again, other than the sheer mayhem of slaughtering aliens. Most games with permadeath mechanics give you some sort of reward that carries over between playthroughs. Space Beast Terror Fright rewards you with a small selection of randomized upgrades that are only kept on successful missions, and completely reset on death. (And you will die a lot in singleplayer, as I've pointed out.) Now this might appeal to you, but for me, and some other players I imagine, the lack of any sort of progression whatsoever might be frustrating. A thing that's not really a genuine criticism of the game but just an odd design choice is that FOV distortion and muzzle flare are initially absolutely ridiculous. You're going to have to tune it way down in the settings to be able to see
I imagine this will be adjusted on full release. (Keys are also not rebindable as of now, but seeing as the controls are surprisingly simple and intuitive, this isn't really a problem.)
Overall Space Beast Terror Fright is a breath of fresh air in the FPS genre that is definitely worth experiencing, despite its issues.

TLDR: A pretty fun game to play with friends. Looking forward to new updates in the future. Definitely filled the hole in my heart that was ripped open by Aliens: Colonial Marines.
As we made our way through the decrepit halls of the ship, the lack of engagements only allowed our fear and anxiety to grow. We had gone a full 6 minutes with no enemy contact. Our plan was simple: Get in, Get the data cores, disrupt the coolant systems to cause a core overload, get out before we become space dust. Breach after Breach was detected, yet no creatures had stood in our path. We activated each sentry unit we came across and closed each door to ensure we would not get attacked from behind, but it wasn't enough. As we collected our first data core, we heard them. They came upon us like a storm, a storm of claws and teeth. The smashing and scraping sounds seemed to eminate from all around us. The screams were the worst part. Those maddening screams. They tore through our Lieutenant almost immediately, the poor sap had his back to the door. I almost threw up in my power suit when we heard the crunching and slurping noises coming from his still activated coms. The remaining 3 of us turn and ran, trying as hard as we could to stay ahead of the scourge. We held up in a hallway under a sentry turret, its firepower adding to our diminished numbers. Just as the fight seemed to turn in our favor, a xenomorph burst through the blast door to our right and slaughtered my remaining 2 teammates. I decimated it with a single shotgun blast to the head but it was too late for my comrades. With my ammo depleted, team wiped out, and power armor damaged to the point of borderline function, I took off at a run towards where we boarded. This damn ship is a maze, with no rhyme or reason to its layout. I found a dead end corridor to rest in, knowing the enemy in pursuit would at least have to come from in front of me. This will be my last broadcast. I can hear them coming. To anyone out there who might recieve this transmission, please... avenge us.

Essentially it's a turn-based game where each player takes their turn simulataneously. The pieces (soldiers) are set, their movfed choreographed and the round is then played out. The aim is to kill the other team before they kill you. It's very tactical and a lot of fun as you squirm in your seat, hoping the enemy team didn't place a sniper around the next corner.
With friends it's a really great time.
Get it if you're looking for something like this, but as I said, make sure it's on sale.

Metal Gear Solid is one of the most well known video game franchises out there. Hideo Kojima has been releasing games under the Metal Gear franchise each of them getting critical acclaim from gamers and critics. The man knows how to tell a story and how to set up a good game without a doubt. Sadly, I haven't played any of them since I grew up with Xbox and when I got my PC it turns out the only MGS game out there was this one and none of the previous titles, and I wanted to do so before I played any of the games.. I could pick up the HD rereleases on my Xbox 360, yeah, but I'm kind of too lazy to go out to GameStop to do it, so yeah. But I watched the trailer for Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain and I was impressed. So I preordered it the day before it came out, which got me a pretty interesting documentary piece before it and this game. MGSV Ground Zeroes. I thought about getting this game a while back, but the Angry Joe review kind of turned me off from it. But since I got it, I figured why the hell not play it? So how was it? Well, let's get into it.
STORY: The year is 1975. Snake is sent into Camp Omega, an American black site on Cuban soil, to extract two people: Paz, a double agent who has worked with Snake, and Chico, a small boy who Snake is training. I'd go into details of it a bit, but I don't really want to spoil much. The story is pretty freaking good, though it is short. Like, really short. I, as someone who isnt that good at stealth games, beat the game in 45 minutes. I heard of guys beating the main game in six minutes. That is... unimpressive, lets say.
GAMEPLAY: From what I know, this is the usual MGS gameplay style. Snake carries a silenced assault rifle and a sleep dart pistol at first, though as you play through you unlock more weapons. I'd highly recommend stealth for this game, at least the main mission, though both ways at playing are fun. Gunplay works well enough, and stealth is decent. If you're detected by an enemy, you go into a reflex mode, which slows down time and lets you take the guy out before he alerts the whole base. This saved me a lot of times, but if you dont think you'd enjoy it you can turn it off. The gameplay overall works well, I have to admit.
GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE: Holy crap this game looks good. I run this game on Medium and I am still really impressed by them. Water reflects off the character's clothing, the lighting is impressive on the main night map and all the other ones, the landscape of the base is nice, overall the game looks great. Plays well, too. Framerate is playable even on my crappy rig, and it's optimized well.
CHARACTERS AND VOICE ACTING: Snake is voiced by Keifer Sutherland instead of the guy who played him before, David Hayter. I think it's a decent replacement, he does a good job as Snake. The other characters are well voice acted as well, Tara Strong as Paz is good, that kid who plays Chico, I forget his name and I'm too lazy to look it up, he did good, Miller's voice actor does good, overall it's good. Character design is nice too and the characters overall are decent.
EXTRAS: You unlock extra challenges when you beat the main game, which put you back into the base and have you do a specific task, like kill some people or save a prisoner. They add a bit of length to the game, and the fact that Hideo Kojima himself is in one of these is amazing, they're kind of underwhelming. You unlock cassettes throughout these modes which explain some backstory and there are little badges that you can collect around the map. These will buff out the already unimpressive gametime, but ah well, it doesn't matter.
FINAL VERDICT: This is basically a five dollar prologue to an epic game sold initially as a $40 full release. Granted they put it down to $30, and the Steam release is down to $20 now, but still, I don't think it's worth it for $20 necessarily. The game goes on sale for $5 often enough, so pick it up then. Maybe see if you can get it alongside The Phantom Pain. Regardless, 8.5/10, it's good for what it is. If you're getting MGS5, pick this up alongside it and play it beforehand. It's a decent enough game and it sets up things to happen in The Phantom Pain. Otherwise, wait for it to go on sale.

This one is pretty original and addictive.
Its a 2D space shooter with RPG / progression elements.
The original part is that the RPG elements are all in the design of your ship.  You'll progress by designing better shaped and more capable craft as you go, and the designing mode itself is a lot of fun.

I like this game, but it gets stale very quickly and the developer didn't deliver on the promises made during early access.  The game is exactly the same as it was when it came out on Steam, with the only major addition being a "tournament" mode where you plop a couple ships into a ladder to see which one wins out.
The aesthetic is interesting, but ultimately the actual game is shallow.  Most of the gameplay comes from designing your ship and seeing how it fares in combat, but the combat is doesn't have strategic depth other than ramming or kiting.  Your design slowly moves away from what you'd call an actual spaceship and more towards a geometric shape with internal engines.  A basic square filled with as many weapons and shields as possible is simply better than trying to create anything that's actually interesting.  Ship combat, therefore, devolves into a blob of shields mounted on a square careening through space and slamming into other blobs of shields in an orgy of lasers and missiles.  It looks nice, but carefully designing a ship isn't worth the effort.
The design system is simple and easy to understand, but in practice it just falls flat.
The "living world" is also not really what you'd expect.  Capturing territory across the galaxy becomes an exercise in Exterminatus from Warhammer 40,000.  You bring as many ships as possible and cleanse every single enemy ship from an area of the map, which then switches colour to your faction.  That's it.  You don't get any resources, your own ships don't start to spawn there, not even a message appears on screen.  A part of the map changes colour, and you move on to the next area.  Eventually this devolves into chasing one tiny little gnat of a ship that can't even hurt you across your territory because it keeps reclaiming tiles.  It's tedious.
Don't get me wrong, I liked this game, but it is very shallow and the replayability just isn't there.
It's fun but confusing at the start.

Creativity in video games has always been a standard. How do you beat this next boss? How do you navigate past this obstacle? In the past, the solution usually had a few different answers, but today the answers offered really do seem endless. Reassembly demostrates this by placing you in a gigantic galactic sandbox. You will start as the little fish, and work your way into becoming a devastating war-machine. Do you prefer anti-matter cannons, or a nice simple plasma beam? Maybe you will swarm the enemies with missiles and drones. Maybe even all of the above! Eventually you will also get the opportunity to design and produce your own fleet with a factory attachment. Each ship can be given a “child order” in which they will spawn their own new ships as long as they too have a factory attached. A war-machine and a loving mother? Oh the duality of man… Er, woman… Err… Spaceship. This isn’t going well. Anyways, let’s take a closer look at Reassembly.
Upon killing an enemy ship you will start to gain “R” or resources, which can then be traded in for “C” (currency). The currency is then used to buy new parts that can be used in any new ship design, this means you will probably redesign your ships fairly regularly to keep up with the latest, greatest weapons in attempts to conquer bigger threats. Your mothership has a “P” limit, I assume P is for power, which can be upgraded with the currency. The power limit of any ship designs constructed will translate to the resource cost once you eventually unlock the factory. While the basics can take a while to master due to the needlessly abbreviated names, eventually your mother-ship will be ready to take on anything. You will scoot around repairing damaged stations, which are actually destroyed by your enemies in real time! There are 7 factions, which means 6 different races to destroy! While you might enjoy feeding on their little guys, stay on your guard because there is almost always a bigger fish. Then again, it might be worth the risk because destroying one of the gigantic capital ships among their allied swarm is extremely thrilling!
Maintaining control of an entire galaxy is tough work though, and opposing factions aren’t the only ones out to ruin your rampage. Agent fleets, which are created and uploaded by other users (via wormholes) will relentlessly hunt down and destroy your spawning stations. When you finally find your way back to try and repair it, prepare for one hell of a fight. Flight and weapons are wonderfully dynamic, both in combat and out. Navigating an asteroid field takes a lot of foresight, unless you just have a set of lasers mounted to burn through anything that gets in your way. Some weapons are able to follow your cursor, while others are mounted firmly to the ship. Finding the best combination for your race, fleet, and strategy is absolutely imperative. Each of the seven races offers a completely unique set of parts for their ships so even after you’ve cleaned up the galaxy as one team, there is still tons of incentive to go back and try the others. The AI is pretty intelligent as well. You won’t see a drone ship (yours or the enemy’s) rush into the fray, and even the combat fighters know when it’s time to retreat.
There is very little criticism I’m able to find for Reassembly. It does lack a story, and the level generation seems completely random which doesn’t lead to much strategy regarding which colored enemies to go after until later in the game when territories have more or less been established. Overall, I found Reassembly to be an endlessly replayable treat, with a learning curve much higher than one would perceive at first glance. There are so many little touches that put this game over the top, such as the ship building battle simulator, in which you can test your newly constructed ship against enemies of around the same cost. This helps immensely with knowing how the AI will handle the many ships you spawn for it. Paired with the amazing construction, and as many galaxies as there are wormholes to crawl through (read: ENDLESS) this game is a fantastic indie gem that has truly blessed my library. Big thanks to Anisoptera Games and Indie Voyage for the review copy, this game is a jump away from absolute perfection. Fantastic work!

I wanted to love this game, I really did. But the glaring flaws with the story, alongside with the inconsistencies in plot and development only leave me wishing that the person who wrote this spent more time learning proper plot structure, than letting the musical work and art of others go to waste. The half baked and poorly delivered plot build up, to the main characters friend psychotic break and unrealistic development only destroyed whatever feeling I was meant to feel, when the forced death scene came around (I'll go into that plot thread later into the review)
Not even  that was my major problem, but it was the fact that from a narrative standpoint, our character goes from someone we'd best believe and understand as an underdog, a man that overcomes all odds and turns a new leaf taking a deep plunge into a character arc that completes the story and leaves you with a bittersweet taste in your mouth.
Instead I get to see a coward, lead a 12 yearold girl to her death all so he can kill someone who was completely justified in wanting to end his life. (even this is debatable since the story doesn't add up and only exists to justify his obsession. This is itself is a gaping plothole.)
Am I really supposed to think, that this thief and murderer (Main character) Is supposed to be seen as a hero when he lets this young girl sacrifice herself over his own ♥♥♥♥up?
This alone also gets worsened, when you realise that her tribe is long dead and gone. Considering the betrayal that sent many a man to his death on the battle that caused the redcoats to desert. ON TOP of the fact that she herself explicitly stated that many were shot and wounded during her capture, making it unlikely and impossible for her tribe to have survived the raids and coercion into the war.
Even the main villain suffers from consistency issues, since he was supposed to be obsessed and abusive. The problem with this was, he was in part going above and beyond with his orders, and sending his men off into a death march into the woods with dwindling food and water reserves. Considering the redcoats desertion, and the broken morale. Even a bluecoat would've deserted. So it completely rocks off the hold and progress, that this man would've made to find and kill his own treatorous friend. Since his scouts and infantry would've left him out in the cold with a gunshot in his chest.
I can't even begin to get started with the confusing dream sequences that seemed to hint that the main character was developing feelings for this 12 yearold girl, only for the writer to realise this was looking really bad, then tip toe and dance away from the dream developments. Alongside the hinted at banter between the two that was only an inch closer to turning romantic, from platonic.
I'm sure that if he thought about this plot a lot more, we would've had this awesome two worlds collide, and interactions that would've left an impact. With a wounded soldier having to repent for past sins, while leaving impactful words on a girl seeing the world torn apart from the evils of man, and the destruction of her manipulated tribe.
But I received none of that, only a half cocked forced plot development. (Her death) and the forced revenge story from the main character (If you start at the beginning and pay attention, he's retelling a story of his partner leaving with half the loot, as he turns away from a life of crime and boards a ship that gets raided by the redcoats. This is the main development that forces him into the army.)
Her death, left me feeling sour for all the wrong reasons. I should've left crying, not asking why at every corner for how bad the developments were to that point, and how forced it was. I can't recommend this visual novel.

Despite my taste for reading, I've never been particularly drown to Visual Novels - probably because I don't consider them exactly as games. Until one day I discovered
(available review
) : an excellent compromise between RPG and Visual Novel. It made me realize what a great adventure it can be : instead of staring at black on white books, you get to experience a story through not only text, but also pictures, musics, sounds, animations, sometimes even choices (note that it's not the case here); and that's what Over The Hills And Far Away has to offer : a marvelous and emotional tale to delight your mind, your eyes, your ears and your hearth.
I would definitely recommend Over The Hills And Far Away if you like Visual Novels, reading or great stories, especially if you can get it on sale. I would have liked a longer story, because I would like to know more about the Shawnee folklore and the last part feels a bit rushed. The journey would have been even better if we had the opportunity to make choices (maybe even alternative endings ?). However, this visual novel remains enjoyable all the way through - a fantastic story to remember.

A story that ends with a beginning. Even though I saw the ending coming (the foreshadowing was on point), that did not make me shed fewer tears; perhaps it was even greater, the pain of the inevitable. I really liked how the game incorporated the Injun speak, and provided a thought-provoking introspective view of two different sides of this tumultuous period. A story to be remembered.

A carefully written and well-written kinetic novel.  I want to emphasize that this is NOT a game per se, but rather a visual novel, a kind of illustrated story that progresses at the reader's pace.  Since it is a kinetic novel, I don't want to give spoilers in this review, but what I can say is that this novel is set during the War of 1812 in the Old Northwest, the region now comprising Michigan, Ohio, Indiana and Illinois.  The precise timeframe is not long after the Battle of the Thames, the battle that destroyed the British army in the western territories and secured the American hold on the original West of the country, laying the foundations for the full Westward expansion of the American people after the way.  It will be of interest to those who like history but don't know much about the history of the Old Northwest.  I think that it will be well-liked by anyone who likes carefully research and well-plotted historical fiction.  It is a bit short, but I think worth the purchase nonetheless.

This definitely won't be for everyone, but strategy enthusiasts will definitely enjoy.

Wasted opportunity. Ancient Rome is such a fertile ground for games, this could have been a great game, but it's mostly a caricature of the Roman Empire. The level design and the story are the definition of linear; the writing is succinct but superficial; the gameplay is numbingly repetitive and elaborately streamlined; the controls are occasionally wonky, probably the result of a rushed PC port; the graphics are not exactly stunning. Its few good moments in character engagement (the forearm handshakes between Vitallion and Marius) and flavour text or local colour (a Cicero quotation in Latin on a wall) are lost in the fray of identical corridors and streets and hundreds of cloned barbarian attackers. At least the single-player campaign is mercifully short, but if it were a better game it could stand to be longer.
As one reviewer noted, this is a shallow and unambitious tech demo, typical for a console launch exclusive (at the time). Maybe pick it up on a sale if it's less than a tenner and give it a roll for a few hours of mindless button-mashing hack-and-slashing, but don't expect more than that.

Excellent game for fans of comic books and/or performing various types of violence upon sytlized bad guys. Plus it's free. Plus you can throw trucks at people. Plus you can set them on fire after you throw the truck at them. Plus you can wear tights while doing so.
Adding onto this with some more detail. Let's look at this from the three core areas I see in the game: Design, Customization, and Story. I'll also talk at the end about grinding.
Design
The game is rendered in a cel-shaded aesthetic. The creators did a great job making almost every part of the game look like a classic comic book. There are some sets that give more of a 90s Saturday Morning Cartoon style, but they still fit into the aesthetic. Moreover, all the locations are done in a similar style and the game applies different filters and effects on top to give different moods depending on the story. Horrific dream sequences are made with stark black and white high contrast filters. Mysterious sewers are given more of a squishy feel with low contrast high blur filters.
Customization
As everyone else will tell you, the game boasts an immense degree of customization. You will rarely, if ever, see two players who look the same. Some will fall into standard tropes, but they will always be different and that is thanks to the powerful customization options. As you might expect, you can put on different costume pieces, but you also have control over your hero's body shape. Make your hero bigger, smaller, longer, shorter, thicker, or thinner both overall and for individual body parts. Maybe your hero got his powers in a candy factory and he now has freakishly long limbs. Maybe your hero is the reincarnation of a T-Rex and has wee little arms. In addition, you can customize how your hero stands. Perhaps they act heroic and strike a pose every chance they get or maybe they stand like a normal person. Add onto this the fact that all heros, even the ones immediately available to new players, can choose at least some of their powers. While subscribers can customize pretty much all their powers, free players still have a great degree of flexibility in how they build their hero's powerset. Maybe you choose more AoE or more single target damage. Maybe you boost your threat generator so you can be a better tank. From there, there are specializations that give your powers special boosts. A bit of bonus crits here, a bit of stacking DoT over there, some vampiric aura under there, etc.
Story
The story is a complex subject. On the one hand, much of it is very much steeped in comic book tropes. You have your standard slum gangs, your evil weapons manufacturers, your mystic snake lovers, your twisted horrors from an eldrich plane, your alternate universe where everything is the opposite, the evil robots, the going back in time to stop the thing, etc. On the other hand, this is part of the charm. It is very self-referential and often self-aware (find the "Defender Fanboy" for some good laughs). It never claims to be bringing you the next great Shakespeare but, for me, the fact that you are fighting the big bad evil without much complexity in the plot is pretty much part of the genre the creators based the game off of.
Grinding
One final note on grinding. The game gets somewhat grindy at the level cap. Personally, I don't think this is unique to this MMO. At some point, the developers put in repeatable content that you need to do often to get large rewards. I think the game does a good job with this. Most importantly, there are lots of potential grinds for you to do, so for me it never got boring. Let's go over them. SPOILERS possibly beyond.
1. UNITY
At the end, you are granted access to a group which sends you on daily quests. These quests are semi-random and fit with the rest of the game's quests which usually boil down to "find bad guy, kick bad guy till he falls over". Once you do the daily quests, you can do a special larger one at the end that is usually a little more special although it still pulls from a finite bank of quests so you will sometimes do the same mission again the next day or something. In addition, there is a repeatable quest to go to an arena and fight your way to an important villain and defeat him. This and another level-cap boss are often considered "beating" the game and people usually play these multiple times to get rare rewards like costume unlocks.
2. Adventure Packs/Comic Series
These missions are larger stories outside the main areas you get access to. They give out lots of different rewards like costume unlocks, action figures, as well as Questionite, which is the currency used to buy special items and/or convert into the paid currency.
3. Alerts
These are randomized encounters that you can queue up for. The game partners you with 4 other heroes who have to take down the villain. The alerts come in three flavors based on the bonus they provide: XP, Resources (gold), and Mod (upgrades for gear). Players often go through at least three each day because of a quest that grants Questionite upon completion and for the bonuses they provide. XP is great for characters either under the level cap or for those heroes who have died a lot and lost their stars (which make you a little weaker). Resources is good for those who need more Resources (measured in Global/National/Local influence, which is a nice touch) either to buy gear off the auction house or pay for things like costume changes
In all, the grinding to me feels a lot like how I felt in Minecraft: There are so many things to actually do, that I never get sick of one of them.

I had won.
So yeah, it's pretty good.

THE SHORT REVIEW:
As a fan of Metal Gear, this is a must-buy, but if your a first time Metal Gear person...it could be hit or miss.
THE LONG REVIEW:
Ground Zeroes serves as the prologue to MGSV: The Phantom Pain, think of it as the appetizer before the main course. But boy oh boy it is actually one hell of a introduction that gets me excited for the full game. The first cutscene where it plays the song "Here's to You" is done superbly, and THAT ENDING, wow, quite the cliffhanger.
To be completely honest I really wasn't expecting a whole lot for how long the game was, and I have to admit I was right in some regard. But where the game lacks in content, it will most likely make up in replay value. The open-ness of the level seems to draw me back and try different approaches, and seek out stuff I might've missed the first time.
The game itself is essentially an overglorified tech-demo, but an impressive one at that. As I said before, the game retains a high replay value because it's open, and the design feels very "alive" to say the least. Should you come into contact with a guard, they will alert the whole base, and everyone will be on high alert. They'll be running around looking for you, and ready to shoot on sight until they've decided to give up the search. Unlike say Far Cry, the game feels less-scripted and more "open" to the AI or player adapting to the environment.
If your new to Metal Gear, here might be an okay starting point, and I say this because it's one of the newer games, with the new mechanics and what not. You'll get into it, but going back and playing the previous games might be harder to do. So I'd suggest either getting caught up with the story, or going back and playing the older games because a lot of what's in here is mostly just tease for the next game for us fans.
Now preformance wise, it's worth noting that the PC version was extremely well optimized for me and my Nvidia, it ran at a high frame rate and was still able to look great, and I have to applaud for them actually making a really good PC version. Did I also mention that the game only takes up only about 4GB and still manages to look better than Titanfall and Call of Duty (which require 50+ GB of space)? This is how PC games are done.
Admittedly the price is still a tad steep even at $19.99 I'd say wait for it to drop in price before picking it up, because you don't really get $19 worth of content, in a sense the value is more in the replay than the actual play (but that could be argued). I'm not saying you have to avoid this entirely if you're getting into the franchise, but if you've had absolutely no experience with Metal Gear then chances are the game might not have the same flair for you.
MADE FOR: Fans wanting a taste of what's to come in The Phantom Pain
NOT MADE FOR: People expecting a full-fledged Metal Gear game

Innovated the only mechanic that really set Sid Meier's Civ 6 apart from its predecessor: District mechanics. Combined with factions, a deep world that merges science fiction and fantasy, campaign narratives that motivate the development of your empire, and RPG style unit customization, you have a game that, historical♥♥♥♥♥♥aside, knocked Civilization down from the pinnacle of the 4X genre.
Now that Civ 6 has implemented this same special mechanic, it's really just a matter of price. I highly recommend Endless Legend if you can get it on the cheap!

This game innovates on the all aspects of 4X design; Quests and Ruins give you a reason to push out into the wilderness throughout the game, Regions and City Stages give an interesting question to weither its better upgrading one city or push out and create a new one, Diplomacy isn't free taking resources that could be used to give faction wide buffs to trade, make piece and even declare war, Luxury and Military Reasources impact what you will build and how you develop.  The one negative is the random combat, its not always clear what units will do given an order or how they will move accross the map.
The greatest thing in the game is the rich story and flavour of each different faction, all of which play completely differently.  The Faction Questline is long enough to be a thread from beginning of the game to the end and introduces you to the factions powers and abilities and gives short term objectives.      The factions diverge sharpley from standard fantasy tropes (for the most part) alowing for several unique storyline.  This is a great game.

Pros
- very active community (large discord page for help, formations, bug reporting, etc.)
- very active developers (frequent ingame events)
- D&D using various characters from several genres
- idle game style, leave it up in the background or even fully exit and it will still play
- interesting formations and effects
- leveling system per character and also per item
Cons

- progression is strongly gear dependant, until you accumulate several pieces of gear across all characters, you will hit a hard wall and can only advance using dragon breath potions, each new piece moves the hard wall further out, but eventually, it is impossible to move any further without using potions

This is a kinetic novel, so if you're expecting any gameplay or choice, look elsewhere. However, if you're willing to experience what is essentially a slideshow comic with a soundtrack, I can recommend this one. The art is very well done, though I wish there were more of it. There are 2 characters that really deserved having their own portraits since they're in more than one scene, but unfortunetly they just get text. A couple scenes reuse assets over again too much, and would have benefitted from some new art. Nevertheless, the story is quite different from most in this genre, and fairly touching too.

I wish I could give this game a neutral mark, but there isn't the option. There's good things in this game, but I'm not very happy that I've played it.
Positives: The soundtrack is good ambient music, the credits vocal song and CG artwork are great, the conclusion was very emotional and touching. Including native American language deserves some credit,
Negatives: Having grown up reading Bernard Cornwall's Sharpe novels, and naturally associating the song 'Over the Hills and Far Away' with young British Tommys far from home, I was very disappointed that the protagonist has spent much of his life on the American frontier, losing the potential story of a stranger in a strange land. The story up to the conclusion wasn't the most original and left me emotionally cold, though I suppose the finale would've been spoilt if it hadn't got me a little. Without choices, or the advantages of movies, kinetic novels probably need to present threats and problems big and fast, and  the first 90% of this story didn't do that. Maybe the story from the vulnerable Mai's perspective would've grabbed me more.

A short visual novel that should be included in your history class.
Playing as William Aubrey, a deserting soldier on the run; you hide in the barn for the harsh weather & execution order for deserting.
However you find you're not alone, stuck with a Shawnee girl -May, who has too much backbone; you soon find yourself pulling out all your hair in frustration.
This novel beautifuly displays the clash of cultures, and the awkward interaction between a harsh soldier & a young cunning girl.
The story is good, not totaly original - But far from cliché.
Haven't seen a VN about the war in 1812 (or about war in general), Indians or their culture - However it heavily depends on an emotional build-up to the climax, which might not work for you.
The graphic is beautiful - the backgrounds are truly well-made and a lot of details was put into every scene. Especially the facial expressions.
The music is a beautiful orchestrial masterpiece by Yuang Chen. I still listen to the soundtrack once in a while.
I found the text well-written.
Now since May is a child, and Aubrey is not the most talkative person, the dialoque is rather simple, however that only shows their difference in persona, culture and objectives.
Aubrey's lack of energy for dealing with May, and his self-pitying will make you laugh, hate and relate.
Very short - 2-3 hours depending on your reading.
It could include more history of May's background & culture. However Aubrey doesn't know much about it, and May doesn't tell much, so it'd feel out of place, if there were too much.
Could be a DLC or extra feature for us who got interested.
Some people miss branching paths.
- It would be nice with a longer story or alternative endings.
A VN set in original settings, a little short but enjoyable all the way through.
However like books; it's highly individual how you perceive the story, characters and philosophical aspects.
Or if you want to re-read the story even while knowing the ending.
The story has some similarities to Planetarian - the Reverie of a Little Planet-
Recommendable if you liked this clash between a soldier and a girl.

While the story may be slow & lack of engaging dialogue for some players, the interaction between a rude & harsh soldier and a young but cunning Indian girl is well portrayed by how awkward but entertaining it can be. CG artworks are beautiful, but since the game is short, not so many places can be covered, which I find it disappointing. Among them, there is a villain character from different faction, which is well-portrayed based on his malice & grudge, enough to make me feel like punching him in the face.
For a short kinetic novel like this, I suggest you to buy this during sale.

Premise: First-person, mp/co-op alien shooter.
Playability: Very simple controls: WASD, shoot and infra-vision. No crouching, jumping, reloading, changing weapons, etc. Maps are randomly generated and some variables are configurable. There is also a seed editor that lets you see how your map will look. Game runs like butter, but it can be a bit delicate w/ multiplayer: if anyone in the party leaves during the game, the entire games stops and kicks everyone back to menu. Being alt-tabbed seems to mess with the game a bit too.
Players: All multiplayer modes are up to 4 players. Many narrow passageways, so watch your fire. Friendly fire is punished, but it's not over the top. There is a deathmatch mode, but it feels more tacked on as the game is meant to be co-op against aliens.
Price: $15, reasonable. May be slightly overpriced for what you get, but the game is EA and less than a year old.
Praise: 3/4 Fun, high tension game. Needs more content in the form of aliens, map customization and game modes to completely justify asking price.

Ok..
So this is my first purchased early access game. I NEVER BUY EARLY ACCESS GAMES ok? But after watching a let's play on YouTube my palms started itching, I knew I had to get this game. 16 hours in and counting, it is the best spent £11 of the year and easily the best game of 2015 due to sheer fun factor.
As the game is in early access, I got it just after patch 18 dropped and patch 19 has since been applied. The developers seem friendly and in touch with the community so I doubt they will abandon this ship mid journey.
The game itself is fun, hardcore, suicidal and addicting, but still fun. Think of the second "Alien" movie, "Aliens", combine that with rogue lite elements, a dash of space hulk, doom, castle wolfenstein and this game appears. At the moment you play either of two game modes; Salvage or deathmatch. I have spent 16 hours playing the Salvage mode, not really a fan of the deathmatch.
The salvage mode is simple, you board a ship, download datacores, shut down the ship's reactors to overload it to explode and get outta dodge before♥♥♥♥♥♥hits the fan. Sounds simple, right? Oh did I mention a zerg load of incoming gunning for you hell bent on feasting on your guts? Ah, I probably should have mentioned that earlier then. ;]
As you progress through a salvage scenario, downloading information to complete an objective randomly confers upon you additional features to your suit which can range from additional ammo stores, to infrared vision or a motion detector to your radar, or more. And for every completed mission, you gain rank and keep the upgrades won during the round but ACHTUNG, BABY; if you then die in the next round you will be reverted back to a fresh recruit straight outta boot camp for the next mission. You have been warned.
The game can be played both single play or a the steam mulitplayer lobby system. I recommend playing in Co-op though, as you will need additional guns to push the aliens back just a few seconds more to download the data for an objective or get a sentry gun up. It's always a mad frantic, hilarious dash from point to point. To make matters worse, some of  your capabilities get downgraded if you take a hit. And I really could spend the next 40 minutes reviewing my experience of the game, which; by the way is overwhelmingly positive, but I'd rather grab my gear and go shoot some bugs. What? Wanna live forever? ;]

A solid fantasy turn-based strategy game with a nice variety of factions and units.
The in-map tactical battles are okay, but like most games of the nature, you tend to end up autoresolving after playing a few. The autoresolve system is pretty nice though, not just mass calculation.
The magic system is so light it feels tacked-on, but it might feel clunky if it had more features, so I'm not sure what I would do there. They focused on a few spells, and it's about half and half for being either useless or very powerful as far as the spells go.
The diplomacy system works pretty okay - I got mad that I was getting declared war on every few turns by every one of my neighbors once I blobbed up, but then I realized they were all good empires and I was the evil undead. The alignment system is okay seems to work well for what it is.
The world is historically inspired rather than going wacky and sticks to pretty basic fantasy tropes.
Overall my only big issue is with the resource system - specific resources tend to be clustered around the map in certain terrain areas, and that means pretty much everyone has the one thing they're swimming in and needs whatever everyone else has. Sounds like it might work for okay diplomacy, but then you realize essential functions (like building forts for example) are restricted by specific resources, and it just feels poorly-done. There's a marketplace system to shore up your resource base with gold, but it depends on the other empires selling off their excess resources, so it almost never has stock of what you need, even if you can afford to splurge the money on it. So, it feels like essential mechanics are denied to you for not being in the right region of the map.
I very much liked the prisoner system in this game. You can trade, imprison, release, or hold prisoners hostage from the battlefield, and it feels very nice and you have a lot of choice. The evil empires can even sacrifice or execute them. A mechanic very well done.

I played this game when I was bored in the middle of the night and here's my two cents on it:
This is a game where you take turns picking words/phrases to fill in your insult sentence to throw against the other player. Of course there are mechanics in this game that determine the way you play sort of like a card game (taking first turn therefore getting first pick on phrases, preventing the opponent from taking a word/phrase so that they can't finish their sentence or get a combo off, etc.)
I would say the only negative with the game is the calculation of points. You can build random insults that don't make sense and still get a good amount of score as long as your sentence is grammatically correct (e.g "Your father is you").
All in all, It's a simple 2$ time-filler that provides some fun with stupid insults.

Want a graphical stylish tactical squad turnbased game? Continue reading!..
Gamemodes included with the game is: A singleplayer campaign, Multiplayer and Skirmish.
So what about the story? Well you are a hired elite soldier for the rebels. your goal is to overthrow a powerfull coperation.The story progress through a city map screen where you can click to progress or hear what characters have to say through potraits with a text window.
You controll a team of elite soldiers and you need to outsmart the Ai on the battlefield. You must plan carefully every move for your soldiers. If it goes wrong? Restart and change tactics. The Ai will and can change tactics on the battlefield. (Note! I recommend playing through the 2 tutorials so you get a hang of the game and mechanics before starting a game.)
Gfx, interface and levels ingame is clean and stylish. Levels are clever and tactical and fun to play, They will surely give you a challenge but they can be beaten. Nothing wrong with the map but you can only read what characters want to say but not really talk to them. Also you can not setup your team weapons and outfitt, those are premade for each missions instead.
The sound effects are good and music does what it should. Some speech for the text screens would have been nice.
When you have beaten campaign you can play skirmish. I think the game will be enjoyable for a longtime in skirmish because you can change almost every aspect of the rules, soldiers weapons  and generated maps or why not use the pre-generated maps with other settings.
The game also includes multiplayer. And i can imagine myself the game can be alot of fun with friends for a laugh or two. Sadly i wont include a multiplayer review due to litle time online.

Interface and game mechanics 9/10 (Slick, stylish and clean. Great controlls)
Story 5,0-10 (Story feels like last thought, its not bad but feels a bit cheap with no animated story that is progressing through campaign.)
So do i recommend this game? YES!.. Price is a bit high so buy it on sale. Its a game every tactical gamer should have in library.

These are words, that I read, when I was consider this game. I love Turn Base Strategy games.
"If you enjoy turm based stragegies you will enjoy this game"
"f you like tactical turn-based games, strategy, and futuristic, sci-fi themes, then you will enjoy this game."
The first thing I learned is that this game is NOT a Turn Based strategy game. Turn Based means, "You Go" then "I go" method of back and forth. While that looks different in a lot of TBS.
Yeah you get your turn, but you plan out your turn, and then you start the turn, and both sides play out Simultaneously.
Secondly, very early in the game, maybe the first mission, or the second mission. I've got my guys in good positions to ambush the enemy as they come down. Then suddenly.... the room where my guys were in simply explodes, killing everyone including the VIP I was supposed to be protecting. While it might of been a plot event, their was to my knowledge no advance warning, to suggest a room was going to explode, and if their was, their was no way of knowing which room would explode.
How am I suppose to plan out moves.... when rooms can explode, without simply playing the same mission over and over and over, and memorize all the stupid events that happen.... this room will explode on turn ... x... etc.
Maybe I missed something, and perhaps I should of read more of the game description than other peoples reviews. But I simply could not get into this game, and simply want to give fair warning to others.

Frozen Synapse Prime is a PS Vita remake of critical-acclaimed Frozen Synapse. Porting it back to it's original platform, suggest some kind of desperation. It's obvious that Prime sold poorly on Vita. So... is it worth picking up?  Nope.
Prime is just a reskin of the original game. Offering new graphics, few changed mechanics and a new, more gamepad-oriented interface. The story, missions, music, gameplay - it's mostly the same game. Nothing is an improvement, excluding only more fleshed out graphics. Vita version could be a good treat, if you own the console, but the PC port is a complete nonsense. If you own the original, there's TOTALLY nothing new here. The game can be a little appeailing to new player, because it looks better... but really, buy the first Frozen Synapse. It just feels better, has a better style and mouse-driven interface.

This is THE definitive lego game for lovers of space and starships.
It always surprises me when developers are able to boil the concept of 'fun' down to such a simple, gratifying level. And that is exactly what you get with this game; an intuitive fleet building experience where the fun doesn't stop when you hit the building menues.
I'd argue it starts there. Though admittedly half or so of my game-time was spent afk (as with most games I play), I have spent roughly 20 hours building ships, and maybe 5 actually cruising around. The 'tournament' style mode you can throw any ship you've been building into is incredibly rewarding, and oddly relaxing. Sitting back and watching the Dreadnaught you've spent an hour on go ripping through other people's lovingly crafted creations is a great system that both allows you to test out your ship against a variety of other players' designs, and serves as eye candy to the nth degree.

The game has a concept of 'agent' fleets, in which a fleet designed by other players invades your world. There is a peculiar feeling I get from this game that stems from this idea, and not even necessarily when I'm playing it. The fact that some poor player will at some point accidentaly have a run in with my fine tuned, massive killing machines gives me a sadistic pleasure that I would say is almost entirely unique to this game.
A gem of a game for people of all ages, and now that it has modding support added, who knows what can come out of this game.

Over the Hills and Far Away has been on my wishlist for quite some time now and I finally bought it months ago and I don't regret it.
Pros
- Takes place during a historical period that most people don't care to remember. I searched about it and it's actually a lot more important than people think it is and it's worth reading about.
- The artwork is fantastic. Filled with personality, the details are delicate but rough in the right places and very pleasing to the eyes.
- Since it's a kinetic novel, you can sit back and watch it like a movie with subtitles.
- Story wise, it isn't the most original out there but it's bittersweet and I almost cried. The prose is great.
- The music is also beautiful. I wouldn't mind having the OST. It's orchestra, no synths, which it may not be historically accurate? But it fits.
- The devs also did their research, I absolutely loved how Mai spoke her language, you rarely see Native Americans represented in media and I'm happy to see so much effort in building Mai.
Cons
- Some people may not like that's it a kinetic novel.
- Some may find it too short.
- Some people may hate the tragic theme, especially since it's kind of easy to assume that it will happen.

I love stories with bittersweet endings. What I love even more than that is when stories are well put together, well writen, and keep my attention til the very end which this VN did. Definitely worth the money I spent. Thank you for making this!

I personally like RPGMaker games a lot. You'd never know what kind of an underrated gem you might discover by trying a new one, whether it be an RPG, an adventure or a puzzle game. Yet, there is a small price of kissing quite so many frogs for the sake of finding a prince. For every game that is remarkable and enjoyable, there are 10 games not so memorable at all.
was one of those frogs. No more, no less.
Our hero is a teenage boy who lives in quiet and uneventful Serene Town, with his grandmother. When William isn't forced to either help his grandmother run the little restaurant downstairs, or complete menial jobs around town to take in a coin, he sleeps in as much as possible. That is William's life, or was until the titular witch Xen comes to his village to forcefully recruit town inhabitants to army to support a new war with the neighboring country. A comment of displeasure coming out of William's mouth costs him dearly as Xen randomly turns Will to a girl to make an example out of him and leaves to attend the war with most of the male population of the town. From thereon, William's long and insufferable quest to find Xen and convince her to turn him back to his proper gender begins.
As you may have guessed so far, this is an RPG and not a great one at that either. The setting of the world has an interesting enough outline, yet it is not elaborated enough to be interesting as a story. There are roaming figures of importance within the story without much decent background or characterization. Our protagonist is practically one dimensional. There is the menace of a war going on, some shady characters with their political plots running about and the appearance of some villains without decent reasons revealed for their acts; and all that Will ever cares about is fetching his body back. He is a bafflingly shallow character, alongside most of his companions, popping into form a party specifically with him, without well-presented reasons. The game has a basic, absurd humor about it yet it fails to present a charm long. Both narrative and characterization lack gravely nearly about everything. There are interesting nuances and plot hooks scattered around, yet they lack foundation without closely knitted backstory. I completed the game, and I see that there was the promise of a fundamentally good setting presented without much work. With some more lore, some more dialogues - without crude sexual remarks, genuine dialogues presenting inner conflicts - it could have been way better.
One doesn't expect miracles from display options in an RPGMaker game, yet at least some customization to sprites or some original character artwork would be nice. The game uses stock sprites and pictures that comes alongside RPGMaker so you've probably seen every one of those figures running around within the game at some point, in a different game. That most certainly breaks immersion if you are familiar with RPGMaker games. The lack of any original music doesn't help either. Maps and environment design are somewhat forlorn with vast spaces without much design arrangement. Recurring styles or items, empty rooms, locked doors; all indicate somewhat of a negligence for the setting.
Gameplay is also an issue. Combat system is basic JRPG, yet there are not many combat conditions or skills specific to NPCs to make things interesting. Each of your companions has 3-4 skills that will unlock through leveling but you can mostly force all encounters with bashing attack option if you have decent enough weapons. In that regard, character levels are more or less ineffective too. If you have good weapons, the game is pretty easy. If not, you'll get your♥♥♥♥♥kicked a lot. Grinding money is easy though, if you are to catch an endlessly tedious job near your starting area. Actual quests on the other hand, don't reward well and most of them are not really creative. Some mentioned occurrences are never presented as quests while some actual quests present no opportunity of learning more about their occurrences. Odd.
By the ending word, I cannot actually recommend
as it is. With more dialogue to portray character depth and background story to visualize the lore of the realm - and less gender humor, seriously! - I'd happily turn a blind eye to the mediocrity of the gameplay. I wish the developer the best of luck for his forthcoming games, and hope for a major patch for this one as it can really improve a fine substructure.
